questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to compose namespace-scoped validation with common CKAD primitives: CronJob scheduling, InitContainer tooling, ConfigMap/Secret usage, and network policies. It exercises security-conscious design (cosign verification, TLS rotation) and practical ops concerns (backoff, idempotence, failure handling).

## Key Concepts
- CronJob scheduling and concurrency
- InitContainer provisioning of tooling
- Secrets and ConfigMaps for keys and creds
- Image verification with cosign
- yq for manifest parsing
- TLS sidecar rotation
- Namespace NetworkPolicy egress controls

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1beta1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: image-signature-checker
spec:
  schedule: "*/2 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          initContainers:
            - name: install-tools
              image: alpine:3.18
              command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache curl jq yq && cp /tools/* /usr/local/bin/"]
          containers:
            - name: verifier
              image: your-registry/placeholder-verifier:latest
              env:
                - name: POST_URL
                  value: "http://signature-portal:8080/api/v1/check"
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle large manifest files or many images to avoid timeouts?
- What changes would you make to support multi-tenant isolation or audit logging?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical handling of in-cluster secret management, file-watching, and safe API exposure.

## Key Concepts
- Kubernetes Secrets and RBAC
- InitContainers and sidecars
- In-cluster API calls with kubectl
- NetworkPolicy scoping and TLS rotation

## Code Example
```yaml
# minimal skeleton
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: secret-rotator
  namespace: default
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: secret-rotator
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: secret-rotator
    spec:
      volumes:
        - name: secrets
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: secrets-pvc
      containers:
        - name: rotator
          image: example/secret-rotator:latest
          volumeMounts:
            - name: secrets
              mountPath: /secrets

              port: 8080

        - name: install-tools
          image: alpine:3.17
          command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache kubectl jq"]
      imagePullSecrets:
        - name: reg-creds
```

- How would you ensure idempotence of secret refresh?

## Why This Is Asked

Tests knowledge of Namespace-scoped quotas and defaults, a core CKAD topic. It also checks YAML correctness and practical validation steps.

## Key Concepts

- ResourceQuota structure and hard limits
- LimitRange defaults and constraints
- Impact on deployments and pod scheduling
- Validation commands and monitoring

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: team-a-quota
  namespace: team-a
spec:
  hard:
    pods: "20"
    requests.cpu: "4"
    requests.memory: "8Gi"
    limits.cpu: "8"
    limits.memory: "16Gi"
```

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata:
  name: team-a-defaults
  namespace: team-a
spec:
  limits:
  - default:
      cpu: "100m"
      memory: "128Mi"
    defaultRequest:
      cpu: "50m"
      memory: "64Mi"
    type: Container
```

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: quiz-app
  namespace: team-a
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: quiz-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: quiz-app
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:stable-alpine
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you adjust quotas for a namespace that periodically spikes usage?
- What are risks of defaulting too low on requests in LimitRange?

## Why This Is Asked
This tests end-to-end Kubernetes app design under CKAD constraints: deployments, secrets, configmaps, probes, resource budgeting, rolling updates, and autoscaling. It emphasizes practical, scalable patterns rather than theory.

## Key Concepts
- Deployments and rollout strategies
- Secrets and ConfigMaps
- Probes and health checks
- Resources and limits
- HorizontalPodAutoscaler
- StatefulSets and PVCs for Redis/PostgreSQL

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: api
spec:
  replicas: 4
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxUnavailable: 25%
      maxSurge: 25%
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: api
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: api
        image: yourrepo/api:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
        envFrom:
        - secretRef:
            name: db-creds
        - configMapRef:
            name: api-flags
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "200m"
            memory: "256Mi"
          limits:
            cpu: "500m"
            memory: "512Mi"
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health
            port: 3000
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health
            port: 3000
          initialDelaySeconds: 15
          periodSeconds: 20
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you monitor Redis cache misses and cache hits?
- How would you handle DB credential rotation without downtime?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design namespace-scoped automation, RBAC, and progressive release patterns using standard CKAD primitives.

## Key Concepts
- ConfigMap-driven orchestration
- kubectl patch in a CronJob
- Rollout status checks and idempotent patches

## Code Example
```yaml

apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: canary-roller
spec:
  schedule: "*/10 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          serviceAccountName: canary-runner
          containers:
            - name: patcher
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to architect cross-resource automation in a namespace, combining CronJob, ConfigMaps, Secrets, and deployment rollouts with proper observability and network controls.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob scheduling and idempotent config sync
- ConfigMaps vs Secrets for config data
- Rolling restarts via deployment annotations
- InitContainers for tooling setup
- Logs stored on a PVC
- NetworkPolicy scoping egress to a single service

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: config-sync
spec:
  schedule: "*/2 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          initContainers:
            - name: install-tools
              image: alpine:3.18
              command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache curl"]
          containers:
            - name: config-fetch
              image: curlimages/curl:8.0.1
              envFrom:
                - secretRef:
                    name: config-token
              command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer ${API_TOKEN}' https://config-service.local/api/v1/env?ns=${NAMESPACE} | script/process-config.sh && kubectl -n ${NAMESPACE} annotate deploy --overwrite canary-updateTime=$(date +%s)" ]
              volumeMounts:
                - name: logs
                  mountPath: /logs
          volumes:
            - name: logs
              persistentVolumeClaim:
                claimName: app-logs
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you ensure the ConfigMap update is atomic and avoid partial writes?
- How would you scale this to many namespaces without duplicating secrets or causing race conditions?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates CKAD competencies in CronJob scheduling, InitContainers for tooling bootstrap, PVC-mounted database operations, health probes, lifecycle hooks, and rollback strategies.

## Key Concepts
- **CronJob**: Scheduled jobs using cron syntax (0 2 * * * for daily at 02:00)
- **InitContainer**: Bootstrap tool installation (sqlite3) before main container runs
- **SQLite Operations**: DELETE with WHERE clause for date filtering, VACUUM for storage reclamation
- **Probes**: readinessProbe and livenessProbe on /healthz endpoint
- **Lifecycle Hooks**: preStop sleep for graceful shutdown
- **PodDisruptionBudget**: minAvailable: 1 ensures availability during disruptions

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: log-pruner
  namespace: ckad-practices
spec:
  schedule: "0 2 * * *"
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  failedJobsHistoryLimit: 1
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        metadata:
          labels:
            app: log-pruner
        spec:
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
          initContainers:
          - name: installer
            image: alpine:3.18
            command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache sqlite"]
            volumeMounts:
            - name: db
              mountPath: /data
          containers:
          - name: pruner
            image: alpine:3.18
            command: ["sh", "-c", "sqlite3 /data/logs.db 'DELETE FROM logs WHERE created_at < date(\"now\", \"-30 days\"); VACUUM;'; curl -X POST -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" -d '{\"deleted\":\"$(date)\"}' http://ops-portal:8080/api/v1/prune-summary"]
            volumeMounts:
            - name: db
              mountPath: /data
            resources:
              requests:
                memory: "64Mi"
                cpu: "100m"
              limits:
                memory: "128Mi"
                cpu: "500m"
            readinessProbe:
              httpGet:
                path: /healthz
                port: 8080
              initialDelaySeconds: 5
              periodSeconds: 10
            livenessProbe:
              httpGet:
                path: /healthz
                port: 8080
              initialDelaySeconds: 15
              periodSeconds: 20
            lifecycle:
              preStop:
                exec:
                  command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 5"]
          volumes:
          - name: db
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: logs-pvc
---
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: log-pruner-pdb
  namespace: ckad-practices
spec:
  minAvailable: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: log-pruner
```

## Rollback Strategy
Maintain version-controlled YAML manifests in a Git repository. On failure, execute:
```bash
kubectl apply -f log-pruner.yaml --record
kubectl rollout undo cronjob/log-pruner
```
Alternatively, use a GitOps tool like ArgoCD or Flux for automated rollbacks.

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests the ability to design an isolated TLS rotation workflow that leverages cert-manager, RBAC, and policy enforcement while producing auditable logs.

## Key Concepts
- Deployments, InitContainers, and probes for reliable pod lifecycle management
- Secrets and Bearer token authentication for secure credential handling
- cert-manager integration for automated certificate rotation testing
- PVC-based logging for persistent audit trails
- Namespace NetworkPolicy for egress control and network segmentation

## Trade-offs
- **Simplicity vs. Security**: Using a single ServiceAccount with broad permissions simplifies implementation but increases blast radius if compromised
- **PVC vs. Sidecar**: A sidecar container offers simpler log shipping but adds resource overhead; a PVC requires external log rotation
- **Polling vs. Watching**: Polling with a cron-style schedule is less efficient than watching but avoids the complexity of setting up a custom controller with informers
- **Egress Control**: NetworkPolicy adds security but increases operational complexity and requires CNI support

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: cert-verifier
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: cert-verifier
  namespace: cert-verifier
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: cert-verifier
  namespace: cert-verifier
rules:
  - apiGroups: [""]
    resources: ["secrets"]
    verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"]
  - apiGroups: ["cert-manager.io"]
    resources: ["certificates"]
    verbs: ["get", "create", "delete"]
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: cert-verifier
  namespace: cert-verifier
subjects:
  - kind: ServiceAccount
    name: cert-verifier
    namespace: cert-verifier
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: cert-verifier
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: audit-credentials
  namespace: cert-verifier
type: Opaque
stringData:
  token: "<bearer-token>"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: cert-verifier-logs
  namespace: cert-verifier
spec:
  accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: cert-verifier
  namespace: cert-verifier
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: cert-verifier
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: cert-verifier
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: cert-verifier
      initContainers:
        - name: installer
          image: alpine:latest
          command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - apk add --no-cache curl jq
          volumeMounts:
            - name: workdir
              mountPath: /work
      containers:
        - name: verifier
          image: alpine:latest
          command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - |
              apk add --no-cache curl jq
              while true; do
                # Watch secrets, check expiry, rotate, post digest
                sleep 3600
              done
          volumeMounts:
            - name: workdir
              mountPath: /work
            - name: logs
              mountPath: /var/log
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /ready
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
            periodSeconds: 10
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthy
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 15
            periodSeconds: 20
      volumes:
        - name: workdir
          emptyDir: {}
        - name: logs
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: cert-verifier-logs
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: cert-verifier-egress
  namespace: cert-verifier
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: cert-verifier
  policyTypes:
    - Egress
  egress:
    - to:
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels:
              name: audit-system
          podSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app: audit-api
      ports:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 443
```

```yaml
# Seed script ConfigMap
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: seed-scripts
data:
  seed.sh: |
    #!/bin/sh
    set -e
    if [ ! -f /cache/.seeded ]; then
      # Execute seeding logic here
      touch /cache/.seeded
    fi
---
# Deployment with InitContainer
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: api-server
  namespace: ckad
spec:
  replicas: 3
  template:
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: seed-cache
        image: busybox:1.35

        volumeMounts:
        - name: seed-scripts
          mountPath: /scripts
        - name: cache-volume
          mountPath: /cache

      - name: api-server
        image: api-server:latest
        volumeMounts:
        - name: cache-volume
          mountPath: /cache
        readinessProbe:
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical CKAD ability to implement per-namespace GitOps, use InitContainers, ConfigMaps, PVCs, and NetworkPolicy; validates YAML tooling, apply flow, and status reporting.

## Key Concepts
- Per-namespace GitOps design patterns
- InitContainer provisioning and tool installation
- YAML validation with kubeval and yamllint
- ConfigMap and Secret usage for configuration
- PVC-based log streaming and persistence
- Namespace-scoped NetworkPolicy for egress control
- Drift detection and status reporting via ConfigMap

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal skeleton for a per-namespace GitOps runner
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: gitops-runner
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: gitops-runner
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gitops-runner
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: git-clone
        image: alpine/git:latest
        env:
        - name: REPO_URL
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: gitops-config
              key: repo-url
        - name: TARGET_PATH
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: gitops-config
              key: target-path
        volumeMounts:
        - name: workspace
          mountPath: /workspace
        command:
        - /bin/sh
        - -c
        - |
          apk add --no-cache git yq
          git clone $(REPO_URL) /workspace/repo
          cd /workspace/repo
          yq eval '.spec.path = "$(TARGET_PATH)"' . > manifests.yaml
      containers:
      - name: validator
        image: kubeval/kubeval:latest
        volumeMounts:
        - name: workspace
          mountPath: /workspace
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /logs
        command:
        - /bin/sh
        - -c
        - |
          kubeval /workspace/manifests.yaml > /logs/validation.log 2>&1
          yamllint -d relaxed /workspace/manifests.yaml >> /logs/validation.log 2>&1
          kubectl apply -f /workspace/manifests.yaml --namespace=$(NAMESPACE)
          kubectl get -f /workspace/manifests.yaml -o jsonpath='{.status}' > /gitops-status
      volumes:
      - name: workspace
        emptyDir: {}
      - name: logs
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: gitops-logs
```
